item.title: Saturday Sessions: GA-20 and Charlie Musselwhite play "Crazy Love"
item.description: Grammy-winning harmonica virtuoso Charlie Musselwhite is a pioneer of the 60s Chicago blues scene. New England blues trio GA-20 is celebrated for their raucous sound and dynamic live performances. GA-20 and Charlie Musselwhite join forces for an electrifying blues collaboration, culminating in their new album "Blues Now!"

item.title: Europe continues to celebrate Pride after attack on Berlin parade
item.description: Large Pride events in Hamburg and Amsterdam are underway after last week's deadly ramming attack in Berlin.

item.title: She went to "hell and back" for a diagnosis. Then her sister showed symptoms.
item.description: Megan Kaverman's weight gain, fatigue, high blood pressure and other symptoms were dismissed for years before she was diagnosed with a rare heart disease.

item.title: Flour + Water redefines traditional Italian cooking in its San Francisco restaurants
item.description: James Beard-nominated co-chefs Thomas McNaughton and Ryan Pollnow redefine traditional Italian cooking with "Flour + Water."

item.title: Bombing in Colombia injures 11, days before presidential inauguration
item.description: President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella condemned the bombing and said "terrorism will not intimidate Colombia."

item.title: "Lioness" stars Laysla de Oliveira and Jill Wagner talk season 3
item.description: Actors Laysla de Oliveira and Jill Wagner are here to discuss the ongoing third season of the hit Paramount+ spy thriller "Lioness."

item.title: From busker to Oscar winner, Glen Hansard remembered for talent and passion
item.description: Oscar-winning Irish musician Glen Hansard, 56, died in a motorcycle crash in Dublin this week. "CBS Saturday Morning" remembers Hansard, a friend of the show who joined us for multiple Saturday Sessions.

item.title: How Americans are handling back-to-school budgeting with rising prices
item.description: With inflation contributing to price bumps, many families are looking to save on their back-to-school budgets. We took a look at a spending survey.

item.title: Kanpai! Sake sommelier explains the delight of this Japanese rice wine
item.description: Japanese alcoholic beverage sake is rising in popularity across the United States. Acclaimed sommelier Daniel Bennett at Chicago's Omakase Room explains more about this beloved rice wine.

item.title: Iran accuses U.S. of escalating tensions as Washington plans more strikes
item.description: Iran accused the U.S. of escalating tensions in the region and said it's preparing its own response if Washington goes ahead with new strikes.

item.title: "Video Killed the Radio Star": MTV's impact, 45 years later
item.description: On August 1, 1981 MTV network launched its historic first broadcast. The burgeoning network went from a shoestring budget to one of the most powerful forces in entertainment and music history. Here's a look back on the impact, 45 years later.

item.title: Spain to put containment fence around Ceuta after migrants rush border
item.description: Most migrants who entered the tiny Spanish territory of Ceuta have been returned to Morocco, Spain's authorities said Saturday.

item.title: Exclusive discounts from CBS Mornings Deals
item.description: On this edition of CBS Deals, we show you items that will help improve your everyday lifestyle. Visit cbsdeals.com to take advantage of these exclusive deals today. CBS earns commissions on purchases made through cbsdeals.com.

item.title: Wildfires threaten France's historic Bordeaux wine region
item.description: Scorching wildfires are encroaching on France's Bordeaux region, known for historic vineyards which power the local economy. Château Smith Haut Lafitte owner Florence Cathiard shared how the fires threaten her grape crops and way of life.

item.title: Why did a wave of migrants cross from Morocco into Spain's Ceuta territory?
item.description: A sudden rush of migrants tried to enter Spain's Ceuta territory from Morocco. At least 67 people died in commotion, some drowning or being trampled. Tens of thousands voluntarily returned to Morocco, and Spanish officials say that most of the migrants have already been sent back over the border. Aidan Stretch spoke with migrants to see why they went to Ceuta.

item.title: U.S. and Israel preparing to bombard Iran's energy infrastructure, sources say
item.description: The U.S. and Israel are planning a huge bombing campaign against energy infrastructure targets in Iran, multiple sources tell CBS News. "Israel is unaware of a decision to restart full military operations, nor has been requested of Israel to join any military actions against Iran," an Israeli official said.

item.title: Trump will push for "anti-weaponization fund" if Blanche not confirmed, he says
item.description: Todd Blanche previously repeatedly told Congress the "anti-weaponization fund" was "dead."

item.title: UEFA says it has lost confidence in FIFA leadership after investment plan
item.description: FIFA chief Gianni Infantino had proposed creating a $20 billion company to run the World Cup with private investors but drew backlash that grew every day since Tuesday's announcement.

item.title: U.S., Israel preparing to bombard energy-related targets in Iran, sources say
item.description: The U.S. and Israel plan to hit Iran's energy infrastructure as soon as this weekend, although no final decision has been made, sources familiar with the matter told CBS News.

item.title: Famed climber dead in Pakistan avalanche; search for others ongoing
item.description: The expedition lost contact with its base camp after an avalanche struck Broad Peak as they attempted to scale the mountain.

item.title: Savannah Guthrie asks for answers about mom Nancy after notes released
item.description: Savannah Guthrie said she and her family have been "in agony and despair ever since" her mother Nancy's disappearance in February.

item.title: Nancy Guthrie ransom notes are released, including message saying she died
item.description: One of the notes threatened to kill Nancy Guthrie if a multimillion-dollar ransom wasn't paid in a week. The second, a few days later, says, "She is buried in nature now."

item.title: A brief timeline of Iranian cyberattacks on the U.S.
item.description: Investigators are probing whether Iranian hackers are behind this week's malicious cyber activity against water systems in Minnesota. If they are found to be the culprits, it would not be the first time.

item.title: Russian strikes on Kyiv kill 9, injure at least 27, officials say
item.description: Kyiv said the strikes had killed four people, and the city's mayor reported 15 people, including two boys aged 13 and 17, were wounded and transported to hospital.

item.title: Body of missing girl found in New Jersey river after 2-day search, officials say
item.description: The body of a missing girl was found in the Passaic River in New Jersey after a two-day search, officials said.

item.title: FIFA scraps its World Cup investment plan after backlash
item.description: FIFA is shelving a controversial plan that would have allowed for billions of dollars in private commercial investment in the World Cup after the proposal was met with fierce opposition from its member nations.

item.title: DOJ to dismiss Reflecting Pool vandalism charges, citing "botched installation"
item.description: Federal prosecutors moved to dismiss an indictment charging U.S. Olympic canoeist David Hearn with ripping the bottom of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, saying the damage was caused by "botched installation and not vandalism."

item.title: Families sue Meta, Snapchat, TikTok, YouTube over deaths of 4 teens
item.description: The families of four children who died by suicide allege that using social media led to depression, anxiety and other mental health problems.

item.title: 3 states would face Colorado River water cuts under federal plan
item.description: Arizona, California, and Nevada would take less water from the Colorado River under a federal proposal to stave off a crisis in the river.

item.title: George Santos to try hand as contestant in grueling TV reality show
item.description: George Santos has worn many hats: swindler, congressman​, prison inmate​, podcast host. The obvious next gig? Reality TV show contestant.
